$comment: WALK NODE SHAPE -- the seam between the server that BUILDS a walk node and the client that READS one. Ruling 123 adds `attributes` to {id,type,label,keys}; identity stays keys-only. Ruling 124 puts the binding ONCE PER SOURCE (bind.entities.<type>.attributes, a sibling of mappings) with role-level allowed only as an override, and defines a conflict as a DIFFERING value: the same value arriving at two times is not one. Both sides are scored against the `expect` recorded here rather than against each other, because server-vs-client alone stays green when both drift the same wrong way. Four shapes are scored because they are the four an operator can meet -- an attribute that arrived, one declared and never reached, two differing values, and the same value twice. The last two are the pair that decides the count.

seam.server: walk node builder (S-52) -- server/ledger_trace_router.py :: /subgraph node payload
seam.client: walk node reader (C-40) -- the walk table's attribute columns
seam.why: An attribute that was never reached must be ABSENT, not null. If 'no value' and 'not walked' render as the same pixel the caller cannot tell them apart, and the operator reads a gap in the data as a gap in the walk. `attribute_conflicts` is a NUMBER, not a list: the list is the atoms themselves and a second copy of them on the node would be a second author.

identity.$why: attributes never enter identity -- two nodes with the same keys are the same node however their attributes differ, and a node whose attribute changes does not become new.

conflict.definition: number of NAMES holding two or more differing values (JSON equality) among the atoms reached
conflict.$why: counting arrivals instead of differing values makes a re-stated fact look like a disagreement.
